thread:
Arjun: Heads up — BrightWave is asking for a Dedicated pool proposal but they keep emphasising big weekend bursts. They want a small committed floor + guaranteed burst window.
Katie: Do we have their traffic percentiles by region? that's the starting point.
Mike: I pulled NY/EU logs last 90 days. p50 steady, p95 spikes roughly 3.5x baseline during marketing pushes. nights UTC they go quiet.
Hao: Important detail: they need guaranteed throughput in eu-west and us-east simultaneously, cannot route cross-region for compliance.
Leah: Pricing note — billing for Dedicated is per-GPU-hour booked (commit) with hourly rounding. bursts above commit are billed at on-demand rate unless we offer burst credits in contract.
Arjun: Right. So two dimensions: committed floor (monthly) and burst policy (minutes per day/week). We should propose a safety margin to avoid invoice surprises.
Katie: I suggest commit = max(region_p95 * safety_factor, min_floor) where safety_factor accounts for traffic volatility + pre-provisioning lead time.
Mike: Example calc I ran: eu-west p95 = 1200 reqs/s -> equals ~6 gpus sustained at avg seq len. with 25% safety -> commit 7.5 ~= 8 GPUs.
Hao: Could we offer a smaller commit + guaranteed burst pool that uses reserved spare GPUs from our regional pool? That avoids forcing them to pay for unused hours.
Leah: Legal needs a clear SLA for burst availability. Also ops: if we overcommit our capacity we risk failing other customers during simultaneous spikes.
Arjun: ops risk noted. Proposed contract tiers: A) conservative commit (p95*1.25) with 15 min/day burst included; B) lean commit (p90*1.1) + paid burst credits; C) fixed-limited commit + autoscale fallback to compatible smaller model variant.
Katie: For BrightWave I lean toward tier A because they want predictable latency for paying customers. Also their finance prefers a single monthly invoice.
Mike: Also we should check cloud billing quirks: noticed that preemptible evictions in one region caused us to spin fallback on-demand which pushed their effective bill up — need to factor eviction headroom into safety_factor.
Hao: Good call. For GPUs on preemptible, add +10-15% to safety. For guaranteed instances add less.
Leah: Billing detail: some clouds round committed GPU counts to next whole GPU per hour per zone. That can create a small disconnect between theoretical commit and invoice. Document that in the SOW.
Arjun: Ops ask: can we add a telemetry alert that flags projected monthly spend > committed by 10% based on rolling 7d usage so Customer Success can intervene before invoice?
Katie: Yes — Redwood Console can emit a "commit-drift" alert and suggested actions: increase commit, apply credits, or throttle noncritical traffic.
Mike: I added a small script to estimate commit drift. Snippet: 
```
# rough calc
commit_gpus = ceil(p95_qps * seq_factor / gpu_qps_capacity * safety_factor)
projected_hours = max(usage_hourly_profile) * 720
```
Hao: We should run that against BrightWave's last 3 months and produce a recommended commit + expected monthly delta under 3 scenarios (normal, marketing spike, black-swan).
Leah: I'll prepare contract language for burst credits and invoicing rounding. Ops needs a gating check: we should not promise burst credits if regional reserved capacity < 20% free at sign time.
Arjun: Final ask: Eng Infra to produce a one-page decision matrix with recommended commit, expected cost delta, risk notes, and required console alerts by EOD Friday. BrightWave exec call Monday.
Katie: I'll coordinate data pulls and draft the matrix. Mike/Hao can you validate modeling assumptions?
Mike: On it — will run the model and post numbers by Thursday.
Hao: Will run region capacity check and list possible fallback model variants.
Leah: I'll draft contract bullets and flag any billing gotchas.
billing-bot: Invoice projection for current month: projected vs committed = 8.6% over — sending billing link to #billing for review.
Arjun: Thanks team. Keep messages short in the doc so CS can paste into the customer note.
Katie: Noted. We'll keep the matrix succinct.
Mike: Quick question — do we want to offer a one-time commit ramp credit (first-month pro-rated) to reduce customer friction?
Leah: Finance ok with a 10% one-time ramp credit if customer signs 12mo. I'll include that option.
Arjun: Good. End-to-end plan looks clear. We'll sync again after Thursday numbers.
